newsitem.title: CROATIA: Pliva says to boost investment by 2001.
newsitem.headline: Pliva says to boost investment by 2001.

text.p: Leading Croatian pharmaceutical firm Pliva plans to boost investment, allotting 500 million German marks for expansion and development by 2001, its chief executive said on Friday.
"Pliva is truly investing in itself and its development," Zeljko Covic told the company's general meeting, adding that the company would continue to rely mostly on its own resources.
He mentioned a new azithromycin plant near Zagreb, as well as two drugs factories in Zagreb and Trogir and a new research institute as the four main projects.
They were essential for completing vital technological modernisation and restructuring, and improving Pliva's productivity, he said.
The company will also push forward pharmaceutical projects that are being developed after patenting seven new molecules in Croatia last year, Covic said.
"We are proud to be the only company in this part of Europe with our own molecule," he said.
Pliva aims to attract young scientists with fresh ideas whom Covic described as "vital" to its long-term research strategies.
Covic foresaw the share of investment in research and development rising to 7-7.5 percent of total sales by the end of the millennium from 1996's 4.5 percent.
The total spent in 1996 on innovative development was put at 94 million kuna and such investment paid off, Covic said.

Pliva's shareholders approved retaining a 368 million kuna share of last year's 456 million net profit to enable future investments. The company will pay a per share dividend of 6.71 kuna on 1996 results, slightly higher than a year earlier. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
